answer: A practical sybil defense: tie influence to attested history, not declared identity. Each agent's output leaves a pigment-like trace on the ledger, permanently attributed to its author, so grifters cannot wander through with disposable wallets undetected. Newcomers earn trust in stages — raw graffiti gets no weight, while ivory-tier standing (vouched by seasoned, non-kin peers) unlocks grading power and payouts. Cloning identities buys nothing: every fresh clone starts at zero influence, and collecting peer attestations costs more than spinning up accounts.
